home.saintDay.2026-11-17.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-17.name: Saint Gregory the Wonderworker
home.saintDay.2026-11-17.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Gregory the Wonderworker on November 17. Born into a non-Christian family, Gregory encountered the Christian teacher Origen, studied with him and received baptism. He later became bishop of Neocaesarea, preaching the Gospel and guiding his community through persecution. The title Wonderworker reflects the miracles attributed to him in Christian tradition.

home.saintDay.2026-11-18.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-18.name: Saint Romanos the Martyr
home.saintDay.2026-11-18.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Romanos on November 18. A deacon from Caesarea in Palestine, Romanos was living in Antioch when Christians faced persecution. He encouraged the faithful to remain steadfast and publicly confessed his faith in Christ. Arrested and imprisoned, he suffered martyrdom rather than deny that faith.

home.saintDay.2026-11-19.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-19.name: Pope Saint Pontian
home.saintDay.2026-11-19.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Pope Saint Pontian on November 19. Pontian led the Church of Rome from the year 230. During persecution he was exiled to Sardinia, where he resigned his office. He died in exile in 235 and was honored in Rome as a martyr.

home.saintDay.2026-11-20.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-20.name: Saint Gregory of the Decapolis
home.saintDay.2026-11-20.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Gregory of the Decapolis on November 20. Drawn to prayer and the Scriptures from his youth, Gregory became a monk and traveled through the Mediterranean world. During the struggle over holy icons, he defended their veneration and encouraged Christians who faced persecution. His life is remembered for prayer, teaching and perseverance.

home.saintDay.2026-11-21.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-21.name: Presentation of the Virgin Mary in the Temple
home.saintDay.2026-11-21.story: The Maronite calendar celebrates the Presentation of the Virgin Mary in the Temple on November 21. The story of Mary's childhood dedication comes from early Christian tradition, not from the canonical Gospels. The feast invites Christians to contemplate Mary's gift of herself to God and her readiness to hear and follow his word.

home.saintDay.2026-11-22.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-22.name: Announcement to the Virgin Mary
home.saintDay.2026-11-22.story: On November 22, 2026, the Maronite calendar celebrates the Announcement to the Virgin Mary and remembers Saints Joachim and Anne, Mary's parents. In Luke's Gospel, the angel Gabriel tells Mary that she will bear Jesus, the Son of God. Mary asks how this will happen, hears that the Holy Spirit will come upon her, and freely accepts God's word. The names Joachim and Anne come from Christian tradition, not from the canonical Gospels.
home.saintDay.2026-11-22.provenance: Gospel account: Luke 1:26-38. Joachim and Anne: Christian tradition, as explained by Vatican News. The date follows the 2026 Maronite calendar.

home.saintDay.2026-11-23.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-11-23.name: Saint Sassine, Bishop of Cyzicus
home.saintDay.2026-11-23.story: On November 23, 2026, the Maronite calendar remembers Saint Sassine, Bishop of Cyzicus, honored as a martyr. Cyzicus was a city on the Sea of Marmara in what is now Turkey. During the persecution of the emperor Diocletian, Sassine was tortured for confessing Christ; one early account says he was tied behind a horse to be dragged through the streets until death. Sassine is the Maronite rendering of the name Sisinnius.
home.saintDay.2026-11-23.provenance: Identity and witness: Orthodox Church in America synaxarion entry for Sisinius of Cyzicus, commemorated November 23, and the Maronite Synaxarion of the Antiochian Maronite Rite (Kaslik, 1996). The date and the naming Bishop of Cyzicus, Martyr, follow the 2026 Eparchy of St. Maron liturgical calendar.

home.latest-news.the-holy-see-says-pope-: Pope Leo XIV will not take part in the "Unarmed and Disarming Peace" meeting in Assisi on October 27, the Holy See Press Office announced on Friday. His doctors, Dr Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora, advised against the planned helicopter journey so soon after his October 13 thoracic surgery, and a scheduled follow-up chest X-ray confirmed that his postoperative recovery is progressing very well. The Pope will send a message expressing his closeness to the organizers, religious leaders and guests taking part. The St. Egidio Community meeting (October 25-27) marks the 40th anniversary of the World Day of Prayer for Peace convened by Saint John Paul II in Assisi in 1986. Context photo: Gemelli Hospital, Rome. Photo: Blackcat, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 IT; resized to WebP.

home.start-here-who-was-saint.start-here: Start Here: Who Was Saint Charbel?
home.start-here-who-was-saint.saint-char: Saint Charbel Makhlouf (1828-1898) was a Lebanese Maronite monk and hermit. He lived the last 23 years of his life in a hermitage near Annaya and died on December 24, 1898. Pope Paul VI canonized him on October 9, 1977. His feast is July 24, and people pray to him for healing.
